exposure: 0.0625% Bupivacaine with Fentanyl 2microg/ml for epidural labor analgesia
0.1% Ropivacaine with Fentanyl 2microg/ml for epidural labor analgesia
outcome: Analgesic effectiveness (VAS score, onset of analgesia, total dose, top-up bolus dose, sensory block)
Hemodynamic stability (maternal blood pressure, SpO2, pulse rate, fetal heart rate)
Labor outcomes (duration of uterine contractions, cervical dilatation, fetal head station, mode of delivery)
Side effects (hypotension, respiratory depression, pruritus, urinary retention, vomiting, local anaesthetic toxicity)
cohort: The study included patients undergoing labor epidural analgesia at Government Vellore Medical College.
finding: Bupivacaine 0.625% with fentanyl 2 mcg/ml and ropivacaine 0.1% with fentanyl 2 mcg/ml provide appropriate and equivalent analgesia for labor without causing local anaesthetic toxicity.
mod_finding: There was no significant difference in the mode of delivery between the bupivacaine and ropivacaine groups.
